紫.meaning: A weaver dyes her wool with beetroot and blueberries and hangs each wet skein of <part>thread</part> on the kitchen <part>spoon rack</part> to dry. The colours drip into each other, red into blue, and by morning every strand and every spoon is the same royal shade: <kanji>purple</kanji>.
紫.on: A knight buys the lot to paint his <sound>shi</sound>eld.
紫.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se cheers, '<sound>Rah</sound>!', and wraps one strand round a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin and a <sound>key</sound>.

胆.meaning: On a lion tamer's X-ray, the doctor spots a little green pouch tucked under the liver, curved like a crescent <part>moon</part>. Every <part>daybreak</part> it squeezes out bitter juice to help with his breakfast bacon. The tamer swears that's where his nerve is kept. It's his <kanji>gall bladder</kanji>.
胆.on: His lions sleep in a dark <sound>tun</sound>nel under the circus tent.
胆.kun: At its far end he keeps a rusty <sound>key</sound> and a sleepy <sound>mo</sound>th.

懇.meaning: A shy <part>robot</part> wants friends, so it bolts a big red <part>heart</part> to its chest and clanks into the jungle. A <part>leopard</part> sniffs it, purrs and takes it to the waterhole, where it shakes every paw and pours the tea. It's the most <kanji>sociable</kanji> robot ever built.
懇.on: Even a grumpy <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down for a cup.
懇.kun: Next, the leopard puts on li<sound>nen</sound> shorts and swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles, and they all splash in together.

阻.meaning: A general plants his <part>pennant</part> on a hill to claim it. His rival stacks a crate in front of it, and <part>moreover</part> another on top, and another, until the flag is hidden behind a wall of boxes and nobody can find the hill. Every plan the general makes, the rival manages to <kanji>thwart</kanji>.
阻.on: Then he drags a squashy <sound>so</sound>fa across the only path up.
阻.kun: The general plays a sad tune on his <sound>ha</sound>rp in the <sound>ba</sound>rn.

狙.meaning: A fisherman climbs onto a crate, and <part>moreover</part> a second crate on top, to get a better angle. He squints for an hour, then swings his line: the <part>fishhook</part> sails past three seagulls and snags the lake's only sunken treasure chest. Patience is everything when you <kanji>aim at</kanji> something.
狙.on: His wife watches from a <sound>so</sound>fa she has dragged down to the shore.
狙.kun: He scoops the chest into his <sound>ne</sound>t, and the seagulls cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

挟.meaning: At the harbour, a sailor drops his <part>anchor</part> and his two little nephews run up for a <part>group hug</part>. He squeezes so hard that the boy in the middle squeaks, wedged between his uncle's arms like a sandwich filling. It's meant as a hug, but it feels like a <kanji>pinch</kanji>.
挟.on: '<sound>Kyo</sound>to,' he says, stretching out the start, when they ask where he's sailing next.
挟.kun: The nephews give him a <sound>ha</sound>rp and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines for the trip.
